module.title: Declarative pipelines and change-data processing
module.summary: Declare datasets and flows and let the dependency graph order them, decide what is incremental and what is rebuilt, weigh expectation actions, and turn change events into SCD type 1 and type 2 tables that survive late, tied and unplaceable changes.
objectives: Read a declarative pipeline as datasets, flows and a dependency graph, and predict what each update and a full refresh reads.
Choose expectation actions knowing their effect on bad rows, and place set-level checks where they gate the SCD flow.
Derive SCD type 1 and type 2 tables under an explicit sequence contract, test their invariants, and map them onto AUTO CDC, naming the release or platform that provides each feature.

scenarios.title: Design Cinderline's parts dimension pipeline for the finance review
scenarios.context: Fictional Cinderline Components wants its parts dimension rebuilt as a declarative pipeline. The ERP emits part change events with a sequence number per part; since June a correction reissued under the same sequence also carries a revision number. The landing zone keeps change files for 30 days. The supplier master arrives as a nightly full export. Finance needs today's costs and the cost in force at any past sequence point for restatements. Engineering runs Databricks in production and wants a laptop development loop on open-source Spark 4.1.3. Last month's events include late arrivals, three ties from May and a handful of events whose sequence failed to parse.
scenarios.task: Write the design note for the finance and platform review: the datasets, flows and dependency graph; the expectations and their actions; the sequence contract with its tie and unplaceable-change policy; the SCD type of each table; the AUTO CDC declarations; what the snapshot cadence hides; and which parts the 4.1.3 development loop can and cannot run.
requirements: Draw the graph with each dataset's kind and say what an incremental update and a full refresh of each would read.
Give every expectation an action and state what that action does to a failing row and to the rest of its batch.
State the sequence contract, including where the tie-breaker comes from, what happens to ties from before June, and what happens to unplaceable changes.
Separate open-source Spark semantics from Databricks features by release, and mark every AUTO CDC declaration as unexecuted until it runs on a workspace.
scenarios.model:
### Graph
Landing files feed part_events, a streaming table with an append flow that reads only new files. part_events feeds part_events_valid (streaming table with expectations) and part_quarantine (streaming table selecting exactly the failing rows). part_ties, a materialized view grouping part_events_valid by part and sequence, finds ties. part_events_clean, a view over part_events_valid without the rows at a tied part and sequence, keeps the AUTO CDC input within its one-update-per-sequence contract; part_current (AUTO CDC, SCD type 1) and part_history (AUTO CDC, SCD type 2) read it. That filter cannot take back a part the incremental targets already hold: a part applied before its tie or its unparseable change arrived stays published. So part_withheld, a materialized view recomputed each update from part_ties and part_quarantine, lists every withheld part with its reason, and finance reads part_current_published and part_history_published, materialized views that anti-join the AUTO CDC targets with part_withheld. (The lab's alternative builds both SCD tables as materialized views recomputed from retained valid history, which withdraws a part by recomputation at the cost of rereading every change.) The supplier export feeds supplier_history (snapshot comparison, SCD type 2). cost_summary is a materialized view over part_current_published and supplier_history, rebuilt each update. A full refresh of part_events would reread only the 30 days the landing zone keeps, so that table is protected from resets.

### Expectations
known_op (op is upsert or delete): drop, because part_quarantine keeps the evidence. has_part (non-blank part): drop into quarantine as well; a blank key names no part, so it withholds nothing, while fail would stop every good row in the update. placeable_seq (sequence parsed and positive): drop into quarantine, and part_withheld lists every part with valid evidence that a quarantined row names. Fail is kept for a breach that invalidates a whole file, which none of these three is.

### Sequence contract
SEQUENCE BY STRUCT(seq, revision_no), valid because the ERP assigns revision_no. Before June there is no revision number, so the three May ties are withheld and listed, and finance sees the count beside the table. Unplaceable changes withhold their key until the ERP reissues them with a valid, higher sequence.

### Tables and cadence
part_current is type 1 for lookups; part_history is type 2 with __START_AT and __END_AT, and late changes restate closed intervals, so finance recomputes affected periods from the table. supplier_history comes from nightly snapshots: a lead-time change reverted within a day is invisible, and a supplier missing from an export is not treated as deleted until the owner confirms the export is complete.

### Releases
Open-source 4.1.3 runs the graph, streaming tables, materialized views and the tie check, but has no expectations and no AUTO CDC, so the laptop loop filters rows explicitly and builds SCD tables with window functions, as lab L07 does. AUTO CDC type 1 appears in open-source 4.2.0; type 2, snapshot CDC and expectations are Databricks features. Every declaration here is unexecuted until it runs on the workspace.
scenarios.reasoning: The note validates and settles ties before rows reach the SCD flows, and withholds parts where finance reads, because an incremental target cannot take back a part it already applied; it states what each refresh can rebuild, says what the snapshot cadence hides, and separates open-source semantics from platform features by release instead of by product name.

rubric.weak: Lists tables without kinds or order; assumes every table is recomputed each time.
rubric.partial: Kinds and edges are right, but what an update or a full refresh reads is not stated.
rubric.strong: Every dataset has its kind and edges, incremental and rebuilt reads are explicit, and full-refresh risk is tied to source retention.

rubric.weak: Uses drop everywhere, or treats expectations as catching ties.
rubric.partial: Actions are chosen, but dropped evidence is lost or the tie check only filters the rows an incremental flow reads, so a part applied before its tie was found stays published.
rubric.strong: Each action is justified by its effect on the batch, failures are kept in quarantine, and withheld parts are removed where consumers read, by a table recomputed each update, not only filtered from later input.

rubric.weak: Orders by arrival or ingestion time; history is append-only.
rubric.partial: Uses the sequence, but ties before June or unplaceable changes are resolved by a guess.
rubric.strong: Tie-breaker comes from the source, pre-June ties and unplaceable changes withhold their keys with visible counts, and late changes restate history.

rubric.weak: Promises AUTO CDC type 2 and expectations on open-source Spark.
rubric.partial: Names Databricks features but not the open-source release boundaries.
rubric.strong: States what 4.1.3 and 4.2.0 provide, what is Databricks-only, and labels every declaration unexecuted.

disclosures.question: Can the ERP team confirm that revision numbers are unique within a sequence value?
disclosures.response: Only for events since the June release. For older events they cannot, so the design withholds the May ties and lists them for the finance controller.

disclosures.question: Does the nightly supplier export ever leave suppliers out?
disclosures.response: Yes: suppliers on credit hold are filtered out of the export. The supplier team is changing the filter; until then an absence is not treated as a delete.

claims.description: In Apache Spark 4.1.0, Spark Declarative Pipelines defines flows that read a source and write a target dataset; a streaming table takes one or more streaming flows and processes only new data; a materialized view has exactly one batch flow; the pipeline orders updates from their dependencies, and dry-run reports syntax, analysis and graph errors such as cycles without reading or writing data.

In the Apache Spark 4.1.0 engine a materialized view is truncated and rebuilt on every update while a streaming table keeps its rows and checkpoints; updates are incremental by default, and a full refresh clears named datasets' data and checkpoints and recomputes them.
claims.context: Open-source engine code at v4.1.0 and the 4.2.0 guide.

claims.description: pyspark.pipelines is absent at the Apache Spark v4.0.4 tag and present from v4.1.0, whose exports include no expectation or AUTO CDC function; at v4.2.0 create_auto_cdc_flow is added and accepts only SCD type 1.
claims.context: Apache Spark source at release tags, read on 2026-09-23.

claims.description: Databricks AUTO CDC applies a change feed to a streaming table as SCD type 1 or type 2 from declared keys, a sequencing expression and a delete condition, handles out-of-order records, expects one distinct update per key per sequencing value, does not support NULL sequencing, fills __START_AT and __END_AT for type 2, and has a Python snapshot variant.
claims.context: Databricks on AWS, as previously read; verify names on the current page.

claims.description: Recorded local run of lab L07 on Apache Spark 4.0.4 (local[2]): Type 1 and Type 2 tables from DataFrame and SQL window functions match hand-authored literals in 17 tests; pyspark.pipelines was not importable there.

concepts.definition: A flow reads a source, applies a query and writes into one target dataset, which stores or scopes the rows.
The graph from each dataset a query reads to the dataset its flow writes, from which the pipeline derives update order.
An incremental update reads only new input into streaming tables; a full refresh clears a dataset and recomputes it from its sources.
A named record-level Boolean rule on a pipeline dataset with an action for failing rows.
Type 1 keeps only each key's current row; type 2 keeps every version with a validity interval.
The source-assigned value that orders one key's changes, independent of when they arrive.
A declarative flow that applies a change feed to a streaming table as SCD type 1 or type 2.
Upserts and deletes computed by comparing consecutive full snapshots of a source.
The open-source declarative pipeline framework in Apache Spark from 4.1.0, which Databricks Lakeflow extends.
